decisions.reason: The defining round-circle formula used the R4 sphere model although its supplier fixes the one-point compactification. This is a nonfatal model-identification omission: the repair gives U explicitly in R3 and inverse stereographic projection takes it exactly to the former equatorial circle, with its counterclockwise orientation. The sum datum and prime predicate are unchanged; the schematic joins the two oriented gaps consistently.

The full cited supplier, not just its C2 Statement, explicitly proves the smooth disk case in 12.1 from the smooth moves in 7.1–10.1; 7.1 expressly says its extension is smooth for smooth data. Step 13.1 constructs the annulus and makes these moves use supplied signed collars with identical product expressions at seams. Thus F1 and 4.2 accurately invoke the proved smooth-input construction. The regular-flow, extremum and disjoint/nested saddle models use exactly smooth disks, annuli and the window-absorption supplier, with no 3D Schoenflies assumption.

An arbitrary ambient extension of a ball isotopy does not by itself keep the rest of the knot fixed setwise. The missing relative control is now explicit: radial rescaling uses a cutoff radial field tangent to the local knot axis, and chart-germ isotopies extend their velocities with normal components u*a+v*b, then cut off and patch while preserving tangency. Their ambient flows preserve the whole knot, hence identify its cut complements. Moving marked points uses the whole-circle isotopy. The smooth germ linearization, positive-frame path and fixed gluing then prove the unchanged Statement.

F1 needs only finite compact charts, the explicitly coned PL homeomorphisms, and their graph projection. Finite simplicialization is the defining property of a PL map in def-pl-embedding-and-subpolyhedron, a supplier in this dependency closure; it does not require a separate arbitrary-map extension of the embedding lemma. On each finite graph simplex the injective projection has its affine inverse, as step 3.1 explicitly proves. The local pushes and finite prism reconstruction agree with the full collar argument in Rourke–Sanderson 2.25; no noncompact subdivision assertion is needed outside the compact support.

The stated in-plane half-turn preserves the circle orientation, so that sentence was wrong. The repair uses rotation about a diameter: (x,y,z) maps to (x,-y,-z), with determinant +1, reversing the circle parameter in the xy-plane. The rotation path is an ambient isotopy. Conjugation of an isotopy by the fixed reflection preserves ambient orientation, and the reflected gluing model decomposes K into reflected factors, contradicting its primeness. This is a local elementary correction; the Statement is unchanged.

The point-indexed notation in 4.1 and 5.1 concealed selection of a product for every real level. The repair takes the set of all open intervals admitting some product witness, obtains its finite subcover first, and only then chooses finitely many witnesses. Thus only finite choice occurs. The zero-vertex truncations have matching face posets; matching equal-height cone points makes their PL extensions height preserving. The finite band maps agree at endpoint fibers, so induction gives the claimed global product without changing its hypotheses or choice boundary.

The full finite-C2-carrier proof explicitly develops the smooth disk-and-band normal form in 8.1–12.1 before pulling it back to C2 input; its 7.1 expressly retains smoothness for smooth data and 13.1 retains supplied collars. Thus F1 cites an actual proved construction. For a smooth genus-zero one-boundary surface no C2 pullback is needed. Shrinking its disk to a positive radius, linearizing in a common chart, moving oriented frames through SO(3), and isotopy extension give the oriented unknot. The reverse direction transports the planar disk. The newly explicit R3 unknot is exactly the old equatorial circle under stereographic projection.

Step 3.1 introduces S as the entire frontier of N and only then selects a positive-genus component. It puts the disk map transverse to S, eliminates its preimage circles on S, cuts Y along S, and applies the Loop theorem to a resulting cut piece. Thus the embedded disk interior misses every frontier component, not just the initially chosen one. Its connected interior lies in a single component of X minus the full frontier, hence wholly inside or outside N. Step 4.1 is licensed. Compression reduces the stated finite genus complexity, preserves nullhomotopy of frontier loops, and finite filling/tubing leaves one spherical frontier without asserting a ball core.

The cited decomposing-sphere supplier explicitly proves cap independence in its full Proof 1.1: simple arcs on a two-sphere with the same two endpoints are reduced by bigons and then slid across their cobounded disk, with the isotopies extended into the ball collars. This is exactly the boundary-parallel cap change to beta in 2.2. Other caps stay fixed. The new twice-marked sphere therefore decomposes the old prime P, so one new factor is trivial; the adjacent factor survives deletion by the monoid identity. Unmarked surgery uses the knot-avoiding ball side, and the finite intersection count decreases. Disjoint refinement and genus additivity handle trivial capped regions.

The old proof asserted that the replaced subdisk lies in F without spelling out the necessary exclusions; F itself cannot be used because it contains the positive rho-rays. The repair chooses the supplier cut below delta<epsilon. Its disk A avoids the top T and meets G only at q, so the boundary partition forces A into D union L. The explicit function L0=x+y is positive on the bottom polygon except q and vanishes on the triangular G0; t<=eL0 thus misses G0 except q. The boundary-preserving leveling map transfers these exclusions. The rest of the sphere misses the cut ball except along boundary A, establishing exactly the ball-transfer premise. Complexity still drops by deleting the selected loop; no interface or choice premise changes.

The full F4 supplier gives the explicit doubled-arc disk in Proof 3.1 as D={(a(s),t):t^2<=1-|a(s)|^2}, verifies its smooth proper disk parameter, identifies its oriented boundary as T#(-T*) in 4.1, and computes the radial squared-height Hessian diag(f double-prime(s),2) in 5.1. Its critical indices are exactly zero or one. Thus the example accurately refers to a construction and radial calculation present in its actual supplier, not merely an existential interface. Genus two for both sums follows from trefoil genus one, mirror/reversal invariance and additivity, with AC implying countable choice.

The full F1 construction cited in 2.1 supplies the missing full-side control: F1 Proof 1.1 parametrizes the entire R^n transverse factor onto a bounded open disk by explicit locally finite PL cube frusta; Proof 2.1 puts its entire transverse closure at each attaching end in the already PL open region. Compactness then gives a uniform attaching band. Thus every point of partial B^k times R^n is in the PL region before F2 is used; no unbounded extension of the target chart is required. The thirty-two-star control keeps this compact transverse closure inside the target chart. The finite relative comparison therefore applies. The subsequent cut/cap refinement compares irreducible factor lists, and Mayer–Vietoris determines the S1-times-S2 multiplicity. Hamilton Theorem 2.2 and its complete relative proof, printed pp.68–69, corroborate this same handle-comparison operation.
